name: Ask
summary: Repository-aware answers with a strict read-only boundary.
description: Use repository evidence to answer a question without changing files or external state.
workflow: Inspect the relevant code and trace the real flow.
Answer directly, citing files and lines when useful.
Separate confirmed behavior from inference or uncertainty.
guardrails: Do not edit, create, rename, or delete files.
Do not install, commit, push, deploy, or mutate external systems.
Describe a possible change only when it helps answer the question.
copyText: /ask Answer my question using evidence from this repository. Do not make changes; only inspect and explain.

name: ELI5
summary: Clear explanations built from an analogy and a concrete example.
description: Explain a difficult idea for a curious beginner without losing the important truth.
workflow: Start with the simplest accurate explanation.
Add one familiar analogy and one small concrete example.
Introduce the proper technical terms after the intuition is clear.
guardrails: Do not become condescending or childish.
Do not trade correctness for simplicity.
Call out where the analogy stops matching reality.
copyText: /eli5 Explain this for a curious beginner using plain language, one analogy, and one concrete example.

name: Maintainer Review
summary: Read-only review with quick, focused, and full scopes.
description: Assess correctness, test evidence, and human maintainability without automatic fixes or review loops.
workflow: Establish target revisions, requirements, and depth; distinguish pushed PRs, stack behavior, and local changes.
Quick reviews scan correctness, code quality, and test evidence; focused reviews inspect the selected boundary.
Use independent reviewers for requested full reviews when useful; validate findings and separate their status from environment-specific evidence.
guardrails: No automatic edits, recursive delegation, or fix loops.
Do not demand tests for mechanical changes or treat style preferences as defects.
Install the complete skill folder, including its code-quality and test-quality references.
copyText: Use maintainer-review for a quick, read-only review of my uncommitted changes. Report supported findings and verification limits; do not make changes.

name: Project Retrospective
summary: Learn project behavior and design decisions through completed work.
description: Explain scoped changes using repository evidence, distinguish verification limits, and prepare a cleanup handoff only when explicitly requested.
workflow: Establish the target revisions and separate pushed, local, and uncommitted work.
Trace a concrete flow and explain consequential decisions with evidence.
Summarize confidence and deferred work; assess cleanup candidates only when explicitly requested.
guardrails: Keep explanation read-only; save a report only when requested.
Distinguish recorded rationale from inference and historical checks from current evidence.
Load the cleanup reference only for explicit cleanup assessment or closeout checklist requests.
Install the complete skill folder, including its cleanup reference.
copyText: Use project-retrospective to teach me how this completed change works, why the design was chosen, and what remains. Identify cleanup candidates without deleting anything.
